sections.title: The letter csé
paragraphs: The letter is called (csé) /tʃeː/. Its main sound is a consonant, which is a sound made when the mouth blocks or narrows the air. You hear it in (csillag) /ˈtʃil.lɒɡ/, which means star. This letter makes two sounds in Hungarian speech.

sections.title: Mouth and voice
paragraphs: For the first sound, touch the ridge behind your upper teeth with your tongue tip. Stop the air for a moment, then release it into a quick hiss. Keep your voice off, so your throat does not shake. For the second sound, make the exact same mouth shape. Turn your voice on, and you feel your throat vibrate.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: In most words, this letter makes its voiceless sound, as in (kocsi) /ˈkot͡ʃi/. It changes before certain following consonants through assimilation, which is a change where one sound becomes more like the sound next to it. Before a consonant that makes your throat vibrate, you turn your voice on, as in (tanácsba) /ˈtɒnaːd͡ʒbɒ/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: You may want to say the two written parts as separate sounds. Do not say a soft k sound before the hiss. The sound is like the start of chair. Say it as one quick burst. When your voice turns on before another consonant, it sounds like the j in jar.
